title: Denoising in Latent Space: What to Compress, What to Preserve
subtitle: Today’s classic · Latent Diffusion Models
intro: No additional research update was verified for this issue. Today’s classic is Latent Diffusion: learn a compressed representation that retains perceptual detail, then model it in latent space. The compression ratio mediates computation and reconstruction quality.

classic.question: If the total budget includes autoencoder training and many inference requests, how should optimal f change with deployment sample count n? How would you control decoder capacity to distinguish a representation bottleneck from under-optimization of the denoiser?

blocks.text: DDPM (2020) turns generation into iterative denoising, but each pixel-space step remains expensive. VQGAN (2021) compresses before learning a generative prior; LDM (CVPR 2022) retains a two-dimensional latent space and assigns generation to a convolutional U-Net, reducing the need for aggressive compression to make autoregressive modeling feasible. This is historical reading, excluded from today’s news count. [1] [2] [3]

blocks.tex: x\in\mathbb R^{H\times W\times3},\quad z=E(x)\in\mathbb R^{H/f\times W/f\times c},\quad \widetilde x=D(z),\quad \frac{\dim z}{\dim x}=\frac{c}{3f^2}
blocks.label: Paper setting and dimension accounting: f is spatial downsampling and c the latent channel count. Spatial positions fall to 1/f²; total dimensionality or total cost need not fall by exactly that factor.

blocks.text: The first stage combines perceptual reconstruction with a patch discriminator to encourage local realism. It uses weak KL regularization or absorbs a VQ quantizer into the decoder. The second stage fixes E and D: KL latents are sampled and rescaled by an estimated standard deviation; VQ latents are noised before quantization. The empirical latent distribution need not itself be standard normal. [1]

blocks.label: The paper’s conditional noise-prediction objective (Eq. 3), with standard forward-diffusion notation. Time t is uniform and the autoencoder is fixed. Drop y for the unconditional model.

Explanatory restatement, not a new theorem of the paper: the population MSE optimum is a conditional mean; differentiating the Gaussian-noised density gives the score identity. This requires t>0 and a differentiable conditional density; a finite network need not attain it.

blocks.text: Conditioning need not be formatted as an image. Let Φᵢ(zₜ) be flattened spatial features at U-Net layer i and τ(y) token representations of text or another input. The following uses a consistent row-vector convention. [1]

blocks.label: The paper’s cross-attention mechanism in equivalent transposed notation: each latent position queries conditioning tokens. The conditioning encoder and denoiser are jointly trained.

blocks.text: Section 4.1 compares f on one A100 with the same parameter count and step count. Class-conditional ImageNet curves reach 2M steps; FID uses 100-step DDIM sampling. The analysis compares training progress and sampling throughput; equal steps do not imply equal elapsed time. [1]

blocks.label: My simplified cost accounting: generate n images with T denoiser calls and one decode each; autoencoder training can be amortized across tasks. Smaller spatial area is not an end-to-end speedup theorem.

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Read the method, compression ablations and Appendix G; experiments were not reproduced. The table is limited to the paper’s models, data and budgets. Larger f is not uniformly better, and reconstruction metrics alone do not determine final generative FID. [1]
